metadata.course_description: Original self-study units with A1 foundations, A2 extensions and expanding B1 grammar across seven domains. CEFR values are lesson targets, not certified learner estimates.
metadata.curriculum_principle: An expanding, independently authored curriculum with age-appropriate contexts and CEFR-targeted language use. Coverage is partial at all levels; current labels are curricular targets, not learner certification.

lessons.title: Second conditional: imaginary situations
objectives: Use if + past simple and would + base verb for imaginary or unlikely present/future situations.
Keep would in the result clause rather than the if-clause in standard second-conditionals.
Use the common hypothetical form If I were you to give advice.

explanation.en: Use the second conditional for imaginary, unlikely or hypothetical situations in the present or future. The usual pattern is if + past simple, would + base verb: If I had more time, I would learn another language. The past form does not mean past time here; it shows distance from reality. In standard second-conditionals, do not put would in the if-clause. The fixed advice pattern If I were you is especially common.
explanation.vi: Dùng câu điều kiện loại hai cho tình huống tưởng tượng, ít có khả năng hoặc giả định ở hiện tại/tương lai. Mẫu thường dùng là if + past simple, would + động từ nguyên mẫu. Dạng quá khứ ở đây không nói về thời gian quá khứ mà thể hiện khoảng cách với thực tế. Thông thường không dùng would trong mệnh đề if. Mẫu If I were you rất phổ biến khi đưa lời khuyên.

examples: If I had more free time, I would join the art club.
If she lived closer, we would see her more often.
If it didn't rain so much, we would walk to school.
If I were you, I would ask the teacher.

activities.prompt: If I ___ more free time, I would join the art club.

options.text: had
have
would have
will have

feedback.explanation_en: The if-clause of a standard second conditional uses the past simple: if I had.

activities.prompt: If she lived closer, we ___ her more often. (see)

feedback.explanation_en: The result clause uses would + base verb; after we, both full and contracted forms are valid.

activities.prompt: Which sentence describes an imaginary present or future situation?

options.text: If I had a bike, I would cycle to school.
If I have breakfast, I feel better.
If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay inside.
I cycled to school yesterday.

feedback.explanation_en: If I had a bike, I would cycle to school uses the second conditional for an unreal or hypothetical situation.

activities.prompt: If it ___ so much, we would walk to school more often.

options.text: didn't rain
doesn't rain
wouldn't rain
won't rain

feedback.explanation_en: The hypothetical if-clause uses the past simple negative: didn't rain.

activities.prompt: What ___ you do if you found a wallet on the bus?

options.text: would
will
did
do

feedback.explanation_en: The result question in a second conditional uses would + subject + base verb.

activities.prompt: Choose the standard advice expression.

options.text: If I were you, I'd talk to the teacher.
If I would be you, I talk to the teacher.
If I am you, I'd talked to the teacher.
If I were you, I will talked to the teacher.

feedback.explanation_en: If I were you is the common hypothetical advice pattern, followed here by would in the result clause.

activities.prompt: If they had a car, they ___ to the coast more often. (drive)

feedback.explanation_en: The result clause uses would drive; the contraction 'd/’d is also standard after they.

activities.prompt: Which sentence has the standard second-conditional form?

options.text: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
If I would know the answer, I told you.
If I know the answer, I would told you.
If I knew the answer, I will tell you.

feedback.explanation_en: The standard pattern is if + past simple, then would + base verb.

activities.prompt: If the school ___ a bigger library, students would have more places to study.

options.text: had
has
would have
will have

feedback.explanation_en: Had is the past-simple form used in the hypothetical if-clause.

activities.prompt: Which sentence is a second conditional rather than a first conditional?

options.text: If we leave now, we'll catch the bus.
If we left now, we would catch the bus.
If water reaches 100°C, it boils.
If you press this button, the light turns on.

feedback.explanation_en: If we left now, we would catch the bus uses past simple + would for a hypothetical situation.

lessons.title: Wish and if only for present situations
objectives: Use wish + past form to express that a present situation is different from what you want.
Use if only for the same present-regret meaning with stronger emphasis.
Use could after wish when the missing ability or possibility is the focus.

explanation.en: Use wish + a past form when you want a present situation to be different: I wish I knew the answer means I do not know it now. If only has a similar meaning but often sounds stronger: If only we lived closer! For ability or possibility, could is common: I wish I could play the guitar. These forms describe an unreal present, not a past event.
explanation.vi: Dùng wish + dạng quá khứ khi muốn một tình huống hiện tại khác đi: I wish I knew the answer nghĩa là hiện tại tôi không biết câu trả lời. If only có ý nghĩa tương tự nhưng thường nhấn mạnh hơn. Khi nói về khả năng hoặc điều có thể làm, thường dùng could: I wish I could play the guitar. Các cấu trúc này diễn tả hiện tại không như mong muốn, không phải sự việc quá khứ.

examples: I wish I knew the answer.
She wishes she had more free time.
I wish I could play the guitar.

activities.prompt: I don't know the answer. I wish I ___ it.

options.text: knew
know
would know
have known

feedback.explanation_en: Wish about an unreal present situation commonly uses a past form: I wish I knew it.

activities.prompt: We live far from our grandparents. If only we ___ closer.

options.text: lived
live
would live
have lived

feedback.explanation_en: If only + past form expresses that the present situation is different from what the speaker wants.

activities.prompt: I can't play the guitar, but I want to. Which sentence fits?

options.text: I wish I could play the guitar.
I wish I can play the guitar.
I wish I played the guitar yesterday.
I hope I could play the guitar now.

feedback.explanation_en: Could is natural after wish when the missing present ability is the focus.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence: I don't have enough free time. I wish I ___ more. (have)

feedback.explanation_en: Wish about the present uses the past form had: I wish I had more.

activities.prompt: The buses come only once an hour. I wish they ___ more often.

options.text: came
come
would came
have come

feedback.explanation_en: Came is the past form used after wish to describe a present situation the speaker wants to be different.

activities.prompt: What does 'If only I spoke Spanish' imply?

options.text: I do not speak Spanish now, and I wish I did.
I spoke Spanish yesterday.
I will definitely speak Spanish tomorrow.
I am asking someone to speak Spanish.

feedback.explanation_en: The sentence expresses regret or desire about a present unreal situation.

activities.prompt: We don't live near the park. If only we ___ nearer. (live)

feedback.explanation_en: If only + lived expresses a wish that the present living situation were different.

activities.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses a present wish about ability?

options.text: She wishes she could swim better.
She wishes she can swim better.
She wishes she could swam better.
She wishes she can swimming better.

feedback.explanation_en: Wish + could + base verb is correct for a desired present ability.

activities.prompt: Which sentence is about a present situation the speaker wants to change?

options.text: I wish my room had more light.
I hope the concert starts on time tomorrow.
I enjoyed the concert last night.
I will paint my room next week.

feedback.explanation_en: I wish my room had more light describes a present reality the speaker wants to be different.

activities.prompt: Choose the best pair.

options.text: Present regret: I wish it wasn't so noisy here. · Future hope: I hope the weather is good tomorrow.
Present regret: I hope it wasn't so noisy here. · Future hope: I wish the weather will be good tomorrow.
Present regret: I wish it isn't noisy here. · Future hope: I hoped the weather good tomorrow.
Present regret: I wish it not noisy. · Future hope: I hope will good weather.

feedback.explanation_en: Wish commonly describes an unreal or unwanted present; hope is natural for a possible future outcome.

lessons.title: Passive voice in the present and past
objectives: Form the present simple passive with am/is/are + past participle.
Form the past simple passive with was/were + past participle.
Choose the passive when the action or receiver is more important than the doer.

explanation.en: Use the passive when the action or the receiver is the main focus, or when the doer is unknown or unimportant. Form the present simple passive with am/is/are + past participle: Rice is grown in many countries. Form the past simple passive with was/were + past participle: The bridge was built in 1998. Add by + agent only when the doer is useful information.
explanation.vi: Dùng câu bị động khi hành động hoặc đối tượng nhận hành động quan trọng hơn người thực hiện, hoặc khi người thực hiện không rõ/không quan trọng. Hiện tại đơn bị động: am/is/are + past participle. Quá khứ đơn bị động: was/were + past participle. Chỉ thêm by + người thực hiện khi thông tin đó cần thiết.

examples: Rice is grown in many countries.
The classrooms are cleaned every evening.
The picture was painted by a local artist.

activities.prompt: These phones ___ in several countries.

options.text: are made
make
are make
made

feedback.explanation_en: The present simple passive uses are + past participle: are made.

activities.prompt: The old bridge ___ in 1998.

options.text: was built
built
was build
is built

feedback.explanation_en: The past simple passive uses was + past participle: was built.

activities.prompt: Complete the passive sentence: The classrooms ___ every evening. (clean)

feedback.explanation_en: The plural subject classrooms takes are + the past participle cleaned.

activities.prompt: The match ___ because of heavy rain yesterday.

options.text: was cancelled
cancelled
is cancel
was cancelling

feedback.explanation_en: Yesterday signals past time, and the match receives the action, so was cancelled is correct.

activities.prompt: Which sentence focuses on the receiver of the action?

options.text: The school library was opened in 2010.
The principal opened the school library in 2010.
Students visit the library every day.
The librarian is opening a box.

feedback.explanation_en: The passive sentence makes the school library, the receiver of the action, the grammatical focus.

activities.prompt: Coffee ___ in this region.

options.text: is grown
grows by farmers
is grow
was growing every year

feedback.explanation_en: For a general present fact in the passive, use is + past participle: is grown.

activities.prompt: Complete the passive sentence: The letters ___ yesterday. (send)

feedback.explanation_en: The plural subject letters in a past passive sentence takes were + sent.

activities.prompt: Which sentence uses by + agent correctly?

options.text: The mural was painted by local students.
The mural painted by local students yesterday was.
The mural was paint by local students.
The mural was by local students painted.

feedback.explanation_en: By + agent follows a correctly formed passive verb: was painted by local students.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct past participle in the passive sentence: 'The windows were ___ last week.'

options.text: replaced
replace
replacing
replaces

feedback.explanation_en: A passive verb uses be + past participle; the past participle is replaced.

activities.prompt: The doer is unknown and the result matters. Which sentence is most suitable?

options.text: My bike was stolen last night.
Someone stole my bike, but I know exactly who.
My bike stole last night.
My bike was stealing last night.

feedback.explanation_en: The passive is useful because the bike/result is the focus and the doer is unknown.

lessons.title: Reported statements and questions
objectives: Report basic statements after a past reporting verb using an appropriate backshift.
Use statement word order in reported wh-questions.
Use if or whether for basic reported yes/no questions.

explanation.en: Reported speech tells another person what someone said without repeating the exact words. After a past reporting verb, a present form often moves back: 'I am tired' → Mia said (that) she was tired; 'I need help' → Leo said that he needed help. Reported questions use statement word order, not direct-question order: 'Where do you live?' → She asked where I lived. For yes/no questions, use if or whether: 'Are you ready?' → He asked if I was ready. This lesson practices clear basic backshift examples where the earlier speech is being reported from a later past viewpoint.
explanation.vi: Reported speech dùng để kể lại lời người khác mà không lặp nguyên văn. Sau động từ tường thuật ở quá khứ, dạng hiện tại thường lùi thì: 'I am tired' → Mia said (that) she was tired. Câu hỏi tường thuật dùng trật tự câu kể, không dùng trật tự đảo của câu hỏi trực tiếp: 'Where do you live?' → She asked where I lived. Với câu hỏi yes/no, dùng if hoặc whether.

examples: Mia said, 'I am tired.' → Mia said (that) she was tired.
Leo said, 'I need help.' → Leo said that he needed help.
She asked, 'Where do you live?' → She asked where I lived.
He asked, 'Are you ready?' → He asked if I was ready.

activities.prompt: Mia said, 'I am tired.' Choose the basic reported form.

options.text: Mia said that she was tired.
Mia said that I am tired.
Mia asked that she was tired.
Mia said was she tired.

feedback.explanation_en: With a past reporting verb, am commonly backshifts to was, and the pronoun changes to she.

activities.prompt: Leo said, 'I need help.' Complete: Leo said that he ___ help.

feedback.explanation_en: Need backshifts to needed in this basic reported-statement context.

activities.prompt: She asked, 'Where do you live?' Choose the reported question.

options.text: She asked where I lived.
She asked where did I live.
She asked where do I live.
She said where I lived?

feedback.explanation_en: Reported wh-questions use statement word order: where I lived, without do/did inversion.

activities.prompt: He asked, 'Are you ready?' Choose the reported yes/no question.

options.text: He asked if I was ready.
He asked was I ready.
He asked that I was ready.
He said if was I ready.

feedback.explanation_en: A reported yes/no question uses if/whether plus statement word order.

activities.prompt: Which reported question has correct word order?

options.text: She asked where the station was.
She asked where was the station.
She asked where did the station be.
She asked where the station did was.

feedback.explanation_en: Reported questions use statement word order: the station was.

activities.prompt: Nora asked, 'Where is your bag?' Choose the reported form.

options.text: Nora asked where my bag was.
Nora asked where was my bag.
Nora said where my bag is?
Nora asked where is your bag.

feedback.explanation_en: The reported question uses statement order and adjusts the pronoun: where my bag was.

activities.prompt: Ben said, 'I like this book.' Choose the basic reported statement.

options.text: Ben said that he liked that book.
Ben asked that he liked this book.
Ben said did he like that book.
Ben said that I like this book.

feedback.explanation_en: The basic reported form changes I to he, like to liked, and this to that in the later reporting context.

activities.prompt: Lina said, 'I will call you tomorrow.' Choose the later reported form.

options.text: Lina said that she would call me the next day.
Lina said that I will call her tomorrow.
Lina asked she would call me next day.
Lina said would she call me tomorrow.

feedback.explanation_en: In this later reported context, will becomes would, pronouns change, and tomorrow becomes the next day.

activities.prompt: Nina asked, 'Do you like chess?' Complete: Nina asked ___ I liked chess.

feedback.explanation_en: Reported yes/no questions can use either if or whether.

activities.prompt: Which sentence correctly removes direct-question inversion?

options.text: Tom asked why the shop was closed.
Tom asked why was the shop closed.
Tom asked why did the shop close was.
Tom asked why the shop did closed.

feedback.explanation_en: A reported wh-question uses statement word order: why the shop was closed.
